Messages.Author: Matthew T. Morgan
Messages.Body:



An action is successful when it goes unblocked. If Michael takes an
action to enter combat, isn't blocked and reaches his target, he gets to
set range to long. I don't see what's unclear about that.

As for Bum's Rush not being replaced, that's because it says "Do not
replace until the end of this action." Again, pretty clear to me.

Matt Morgan

Messages.Author: John Flournoy
Messages.Body:


What Matt said. Plus, note that there is a difference between
determining that an action is successful (or not) and 'the action has
ended'; there are plenty of effects that can only take place after an
action has been determined to be successful or unsuccessful that are
still part of the action; one such would be Spying Mission (at
superior).

Plus, you can do fun things like 'I Bum's Rush your vampire, who does
not block; I strike Form of Mist, continue the action at +1 stealth and
enter combat with you again' (not that you necessarily would WANT to do
this, but you can.) The fact that the action was unblocked does not
mean that the action has ended either as you enter, during, or
immediately after that initial combat.

-John Flournoy

Wow, that is actually a very good vampire.
A friend of mine plays a nasty Assamite rush deck with lots and lots of
the long-range-only strikes (Blood Sweat and Tase of Death). It's a
strong deck, it won a 16-player Sydney tournament recently. One problem
he has is not always having manuevers (or having enough). This guy can
stealth a rush action with obf or use a haven and get a guaranteed
long-range strike. Blood Sweat the blood off them, additional and Taste
to bin or burn. This guy will go very well in these sorts of decks I
think. Not as discipline-focuses as say Abd Al Rashid but a really
useful special. Thank god Assamites are getting some strong vampires to
make up for their weaknesses (no intercept, no flick).

Messages.Author: LSJ
Messages.Body:
press wrote:
> just for me to get a thing clear, almost same scenario, a vampire

> rushing someone, but he愀 blocked. he then plays Trap (or conquer the

> beast) and hurts the blocker real bad without sending him to torpor or
> burning him, press to continue the vampire then plays form of myst (or
> shadow body). the original rush goes on and then i can beat up two
> vampires in a row with only one action. this is correct and possible,
> right?

Yes. If you get blocked, you can Form of Mist (or other continue
action strike) during any strike on any round, not just the first
strike of the first round). The action (rush, bleed, whatever)
will then continue a if unblocked even though several
rounds of block-combat have been done (and pain inflicted).
